html:
Raja Harishchandra is a silent film made by Dadasaheb Phalke and released in Bombay in May 1913. It is counted as the first full length Indian feature film.

Phalke had worked as a photographer and printer. Watching a film about the life of Christ, he decided Indians should see their own gods and heroes on screen. He went to London to buy a camera and learn the craft, then shot the film with his family's help.

The story comes from Hindu legend: King Harishchandra, who never lies, gives up his kingdom, his wife and his son to keep his word, until the gods reward him. Because acting was thought shameful for women, men played the female roles.

The film was about forty minutes long, and only parts of it survive. Its success led Phalke to make dozens more films on myths. Sound came with Alam Ara in 1931, and Bombay grew into the centre of Hindi cinema, one of the busiest film industries on earth, beside Hollywood. India's top film award is named after Phalke. Later landmarks include Pather Panchali and Sholay.
sum: Raja Harishchandra is a silent film made by Dadasaheb Phalke and released in Bombay in May 1913. It is counted as the first full length Indian feature film.
